result.title: Unsupervised Head Network Personalization for Split Computing via Federated Learning
result.comment: 12 pages, 8 figures, 4 tables. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication
result.summary: Split Computing (SC) is a distributed inference method designed for balancing computational load and reducing latency by partitioning a neural network into head and tail networks and deploying them across both a mobile device and a server, respectively. Due to the limited bandwidth and computational power of mobile devices, the head network is often replaced with a neural network that requires lower computational and communication resources. However, it is challenging to prepare a sufficient quantity and quality of labeled data on the mobile device side for training the replacement head network. Furthermore, the data prepared by mobile users often contains sensitive privacy information, making data aggregation difficult. In this paper, we propose a data-efficient head network training method for SC. This method utilizes federated learning and knowledge distillation to train the head network using a small amount of non-IID and unlabeled data from mobile devices, ensuring that the training datasets are not exposed. Moreover, by introducing personalization, we enhance the accuracy to levels comparable to or exceeding those of existing methods. The experimental evaluations demonstrate that, despite data constraints imposed only on our method, it achieves accuracy comparable to the baselines. Furthermore, it significantly reduces the communication requirements by 95% on mobile devices, with only a 3-5 percentage point drop in accuracy from the original model.

AI.brief_summary: 提出一种面向 split computing 的 head 网络个性化训练方法，利用联邦学习与知识蒸馏，在移动端少量非独立同分布无标签数据上训练替代 head 网络，以兼顾精度与通信开销。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作处理的是分布式推理的效率、隐私与通信成本，head 网络仅是特征提取前端，未涉及 latent 推理状态的生成、视觉证据使用或推理期决策，与 LVR 主线缺乏具体可借鉴联系。
